newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News Corp asked to lift Seven stake-Howard.
newsitem.headline: News Corp asked to lift Seven stake-Howard.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday that News Corp 's Australian unit News Ltd had in a recent meeting asked if the government would raise its current 15 percent limit on foreign ownership so News could increase its stake in Seven Network Ltd.
Howard told reporters that nothing had come from the proposition and the government had made no decisions on either the cross-media or foreign ownership media rules.

"What happened was that I was asked by News Ltd, by one of the Murdochs, whether I would be willing to agree to an increase in the foreign investment limits on television," the Prime Minister told reporters.

"In the course of discussions with him, and also with Mr Cowley, the proposition was put as to whether News Ltd would be willing to surrender ownership of some newspapers if an increase in television foreign ownership was allowed," he added.
Howard said the government was concerned that the level of foreign ownership of Australia's media did not increase.
"No government decision on any aspect of media law has been taken and I want to make it plain to everybody who is interested," he said.

News Ltd, the Australian offshoot of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, controls about 75 percent of Australia's metropolitan newspaper circulation with papers in five of six capital cities. Murdoch was born in Australia but became a United States citizen to allow his ownership of the Fox television network.
His Australian papers compete in the key Sydney and Melbourne markets with John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, the publisher of the Sydney Morning Herald and the Melbourne Age.
Fairfax also publishes the Australian Financial Review national business daily.
The much-mooted takeover of Fairfax by media proprietor and local billionaire businessman Kerry Packer was propelled last week by meetings in Canberra between Packer and Howard.
Packer, who owns the leading Nine Network television group, also has a 15 percent stake in Fairfax and is the largest shareholder after Brierley Investment Ltd which has 20 percent.

Current media laws prevent ownership of both newspapers and television stations in major markets. Howard said he was not a supporter of the cross media law and had held that position for the last 10 years. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
